Landing.title: quickdraw
Landing.tagline: The realtime fullstack starter for quickdraw-core
Landing.subtitle: Typed realtime services, access policies on every row, a full auth suite, and a multiplayer game foundation — already wired together. Fork it and build the interesting part.
Landing.featRealtimeDesc: Methods, live rows and live lists over Socket.IO — declared once in a contract, end-to-end typed, validated, cached with TanStack Query.
Landing.featRealtimeDetail: A contract declares each method once; qd.defineService implements it with its access and its handler, and the client calls it through a typed hook. Handlers write through the tracked Prisma client, so every subscriber's rows and lists update live — no REST boilerplate, no hand-sent events, no drift between client and server types.
Landing.featAclDesc: Service-wide grants plus a row policy per service (an owner, a JSON access list, a membership table), enforced server-side on every method, subscription, list and channel.
Landing.featAclDetail: Each method declares who may call it (signed in, a level on the row, a service-wide grant) and each service declares how a user's level on a row is found. ChatService reads a membership table and DocumentService a JSON access list, while profiles are readable by everyone signed in — one policy decides calls, live subscriptions and lists alike, and everything fails closed.
Landing.featGameDesc: A Godot 4 snake demo with real netcode: 20Hz input channels, client prediction, snapshot interpolation, server-side NPCs, and React overlays driving the sim.
Landing.featGameDetail: Channels are the high-frequency counterpart to methods: fire-and-forget, schema-checked per message, rate-limited by a per-socket token bucket, and gated on the world's room; every tick's snapshot goes out on a volatile stream. The Godot client speaks the same protocol in GDScript — game commands stay ordinary quickdraw methods a React button can call too.
Landing.featAuthDesc: Google & Discord OAuth, revocable sessions, guest play, a Discord Activity embed — and a mock OAuth flow so local dev never needs real credentials.
Landing.featAuthDetail: quickdraw's auth routes kit: sessions are JWTs naming revocable database rows, carried in an httpOnly cookie — the same credential authenticates every socket, HTTP call and REST route. Guest sessions mint real (marked) users so anonymous players get scores and chat; the mock OAuth provider runs a genuine code flow against seeded users and refuses to run in production.
Landing.featAdminDesc: Every service gets an admin CRUD surface for free — the game's live-tunable variables are edited right in the browser.
Landing.featAdminDetail: The admin kit adds list/get/create/update/delete to a service in one spread, and the generic /admin UI renders tables and editors from each service's metadata — no per-service admin pages to build. Grants are edited there too, and so are the game's tunables (definitions), live.
Landing.featTestingDesc: Integration tests run on in-memory PGlite locally (seconds, no setup) and real PostgreSQL in CI — the same suite, both places.
Landing.featTestingDetail: createTestApp boots every service on a real server: app.as(user) calls in process, app.connect(user) over a real socket. Each service pins who may call each method in an access matrix, and the hot paths keep committed query budgets. TEST_DATABASE_URL flips the database between fingerprint-cached in-memory PGlite (local default) and per-worker cloned PostgreSQL (CI).
Landing.featDeployDesc: GitHub Actions for drift checks, lint, types, and sharded tests, plus a one-click deploy pipeline to Cloud Run and Vercel.
Landing.featDeployDetail: CI fails PRs on migration drift and runs cached lint/typecheck/build plus sharded integration tests against real PostgreSQL. The deploy workflow chains a secret scan, Prisma migrations, a Docker image to Cloud Run, and the web app to Vercel — fill in the placeholders and it's one click.
Landing.featGuardrailsDesc: Strict lint rules ship with the framework and update with it, your own rules are one file away, and quickdraw's agent rules and skills keep agents on the rails.
Landing.featGuardrailsDetail: The oxlint config extends quickdraw-lint's template config (strict categories, complexity budgets, and the quickdraw rules: untracked writes, unbounded reads, raw sockets, removed APIs), so best practices update with the package. eslint-plugin-project is where your own rules go, and quickdraw's rules and skills are linked into .claude/ beside this app's path-scoped rules, loading when Claude Code touches matching paths.
Landing.featForkDesc: init-fork.sh renames the whole identity — app, database, deploy targets — and can carve out the game foundation cleanly if you don't need it.
Landing.featForkDetail: One script rewrites databases, display names, deploy service names, the devcontainer, and optionally the backend port and package scope — then deletes itself. --without-game removes the entire game foundation along marked seams and verifies the result builds before it finishes.
